sense: a guest who calls or stays

terms.grammar: noun, third declension; feminine hospita, hospitae
evidence: Ov. F. 5.502: hospitibus jānua nostra patet
terms.comment: A guest who comes to the house, to call or to stay; at the table he is a convīva (see guest). The same word is the host (see host): the sentence shows which is meant.

terms.gloss: a caller who comes to pay his respects
terms.comment: The Roman morning caller at a great man’s house, and later a courtier (Lewis & Short): a visit of courtesy, not a friend dropping in.

phrases.latin: sī vespertīnus subitō tē oppresserit hospes
phrases.english: if a visitor descends on you suddenly in the evening
and our door is open to visitors

phrases.latin: hospes, hīc bene manēbis, hīc summum bonum voluptās est
phrases.english: guest, you will be well off staying here; here the highest good is pleasure

sources: Lewis & Short: hospes · Lewis & Short: salutator
